function: Learned network slicing for satellite D2D NTN: admission of service requests, VNF embedding and traffic routing by federated multiagent D3QN (p. 5 observation space; p. 6 admission reward; p. 9); above the PHY.
notes: Exclude, reason above_phy. The learned Fed-D3QN agents perform network slicing, admission (access) control and routing, all above the PHY. p. 1: "The federated multiagent-DRL framework dynamically manages network slices". p. 5: the observation space holds "the type of service required by incoming service requests (SRs)", "the embedding-relationship matrix", "the offered revenue" and "the current state of the substrate network (Ct, Bt)" (computing capacity and link bandwidth, p. 10). p. 6: "For the RM agent, the reward is based on the admission of st" (Algorithm 1 rewards only admissions and valid embeddings). p. 9: "This policy effectively allocates resources and routes traffic for diverse service flows". Baselines and metrics are slicing-level: greedy VNF placement (p. 8), interslice cost, active and high-priority SRs, slicing capacity, latency, packet loss (pp. 9-11). For the reviewer: one generic sentence on p. 5 says "agents utilize the trained Fed-D3QN strategy to select power levels and channel actions", in a passage that also speaks of vehicles and vehicular networks; no power or channel action, channel state, or PHY metric appears in the MDP (pp. 5-6) or results, so I do not count it as a learned physical-layer decision under the joint rule. If the reviewer does, the work would pass check 4 as area 6 and need full grading. FedAvg aggregation is digital (p. 5, eq. 17), not over the air. Title on page 1 matches the DOI (p. 1: "Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/JIOT.2024.3479779").
